transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-20 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Miguel, Sara, Ethan (+ Olivia on calendar but couldn't make it)

Summary: Quick sync on v2.3 runtime release readiness, SDK v2 launch items, outstanding performance regressions after quantization, and rollout playbook for Dedicated and Private customers. Aim: agree on go/no-go checklist and owners for last-mile fixes.

Topics: runtime perf, quantization regressions, batcher changes, autoscale/playbook, launch comms, incident readiness

[00:00] Jordan: ok good morning everyone, we're doing the v2.3/SDK v2 launch sync — should be tight, so agenda is checklist, perf blockers, release playbook, open risks.
[00:18] Priya: hi, morning. quick status: the runtime r2 branch landed the attention kernel fixes, we've got preliminary numbers but there's a noise in long-seq workloads.
[00:30] Miguel: yeah i saw that — staging had a couple of tail-latency spikes yesterday around 3k tokens when batch sizes spiked. might be batching threshold logic not kicking in.
[00:42] Ethan: and QA flagged two nondeterministic failures in the quantized path, they happen intermittently under load.
[00:50] Jordan: ok can you describe the failures a little? are they correctness, or just numerical flakiness?
[00:58] Ethan: mostly numerical, sometimes outputs skew by a token or two, sometimes decode loop errors. logging is messy but i put links to failing traces in the ticket — ticket RF-1287.
[01:15] Priya: my hypothesis: the quant path + kv cache eviction race for long requests. the kv cache indexing code had a micro-optimization that may be racy under concurrent micro-batches.
[01:30] Miguel: that could also explain the tail latencies, if cache miss paths are doing extra compute. i'll instrument the staging endpoints to surface cache hit/miss rates and CPU / memcpy hotspots.
[01:42] Speaker 2 (Sara): also from an ops perspective we need clear fallback for Dedicated customers — if quantized builds are flaky, we should have an automatic fallback to fp16 variant per policy.
[01:55] Priya: agreed, we have policy flags but not a fully tested fallback. i think we should add an automated canary that flips the model variant per-route if error rate crosses threshold.
[02:08] Jordan: add that to the playbook. Miguel, can we fold that into autoscale tests?
[02:14] Miguel: yes we can script a canary that injects errors and observes fallback, then measure latency and cost delta. i'll put a runbook in staging.
[02:25] [02:25] Jordan: quick note — we need to be mindful of customer SLAs; Sara, do we have language on what qualifies as outage vs degradation in the comms doc?
[02:35] Sara: current comms doc says degradation defined as error rate >2% or latency 3x baseline for >5 minutes. that's in the initial draft. we can tighten if PMs want.
[02:48] Priya: one more perf note: the fused attention kernels improve throughput but introduced a regression for batch sizes below 8 in GPU mem bound cases. our scheduler currently aims for latency SLOs with dynamic batching; small tail cases are suffering.
[03:05] Miguel: can we change the batching policy to lower minimum batch size for low concurrency routes? but that raises cost.
[03:12] Jordan: tradeoff call — cost vs latency. for launch we may prioritize latency for our key PLG demo routes and leave cheaper defaults for lower-tier customers. keep that in RACI.
[03:22] Ethan: for QA regression, i'll prioritize smoke vs full regression. smoke needs to cover decode correctness, kv cache stability, and fallback behavior.
[03:32] Priya: i'll push a patch to kv indexer today to add a lock and a metrics increment; should reduce races. but there's a performance tax — we need numbers.
[03:45] Miguel: if lock slows us, we can try a sharded lock per-kv-segment to reduce contention — trade space vs complexity.
[03:55] Jordan: ok, so immediate plan: priya implements lock/sharded prototype; ethan runs smoke regressions nightly; miguel adds instrumentation; sara updates playbook & comms; jordan owns launch timeline.
[04:08] [04:08] Jordan: any blockers on infra for the autoscale validation?
[04:12] Miguel: we need a small infra quota bump to test higher concurrency in staging — i submitted request but want signoff. cost estimate about $400 for the week of testing.
[04:24] Sara: ops budget ok with that for launch testing, we just need the spend code.
[04:30] Jordan: i'll approve. please add cost notes to the launch doc.
[04:34] [04:34] Jordan: security and compliance check — do we have any outstanding items for Private deployments?
[04:39] Priya: we have the KMS integration in place but the audit logs for model access need an additional field (model_version) that security asked for.
[04:48] Ethan: added a ticket RF-1299 to add model_version to audit events; QA will validate once the logs appear in staging.
[04:56] Miguel: also verify HSM key rotation path in staging, i had a failure when rotating keys last month in the private env.
[05:06] Jordan: mark that as high priority for Private customers, include in the incident runbook.
[05:12] Priya: labeling risk items: 1) quantization nondet (high), 2) batching tail latency (medium-high), 3) audit log missing field (medium), 4) autoscale test infra quota (low).
[05:26] Speaker 3 (Ethan): question — for SDK v2, are we shipping the new streaming API by GA or is that a beta?
[05:34] Jordan: plan is GA with streaming, but with opt-in flags for older clients. we need migration notes and a deprecation schedule.
[05:42] Sara: we should include a migration checklist and sample code. i'll coordinate with developer advocacy.
[05:48] Priya: developer-facing behavior also depends on runtime change to chunked kv delivery — we need tests to ensure no regressions for clients that rely on immediate KV reads.
[06:00] Jordan: good call. priya, add a client compatibility test matrix to the checklist.
[06:06] Priya: will do.
[06:08] [06:08] Jordan: timeline check — we are aiming to cut release candidate on 2025-06-27, final GA 2025-07-02. is that still realistic?
[06:18] Miguel: rc cut is okay if we resolve the quant nondet within a week, otherwise we should delay.
[06:24] Ethan: QA can accelerate some tests but the nondet will need dev fix + 48 hours of validation.
[06:30] Jordan: decision point: if quant nondet not fixed by 2025-06-25, we postpone GA by a week and do a canary with fp16 as default for Dedicated.
[06:42] Sara: i'll draft the comms for both paths (on-time GA vs one-week delay) so we're ready.
[06:48] Priya: final note on telemetry — we need to tag rollout with experiment IDs to compare model variants and quantify cost delta per-token.
[06:56] Miguel: i'll add telemetry fields and a dashboard stub in Grafana with cost / latency / error-rate curves.
[07:04] Jordan: ok let's recap: priya perf patch + metrics by end of day 6/20, miguel staging instrumentation + autoscale playbook, ethan nightly smoke/regressions, sara playbook & comms, jordan final launch doc and approver list. owners and dates in action items.
[07:25] [07:25] Jordan: anything else?
[07:29] Priya: please add RF-1287 and RF-1299 to the release blocker list in the tracker.
[07:36] Jordan: will do. thanks everyone, we'll reconvene on 6/23 for a status update.

References / Links shared: launch-plan doc (internal link), RF-1287 (quant nondet), RF-1299 (audit log), benchmark spreadsheet (staging perf runs), autoscale playbook draft (staging runbook).

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few mis-recognitions ("KV cache" sometimes split, "Dedicated" appeared as "decided" once), speaker labels occasionally generic. Kept original speech patterns and filler words.
